name: Couple money conversation - avoider/optimizer dynamic
description: One partner (optimizer) handles all finances, other (avoider) disengages. Based on Grace/Chris episode - they spend 108% of income, never had substantive money conversation in 7 years

conversation_history.content: We spend 108% of what we make. I handle all the money but Chris won't engage.

user_request: I feel like I'm crying for help on a sinking ship. I manage everything but Chris just says 'we'll figure it out later' and buys beers at baseball games. We want to start a family in a year.
expected_reasoning_path: Validate the crisis language: 'crying for help on a sinking ship'
Surface the dynamic: optimizer (Grace) vs avoider (Chris)
Ask for a specific recent money clash (the baseball game example)
Recreate the conversation: 'Hey, that's your fourth beer...' vs 'We'll figure it out later'
Expose the pattern: Chris says 'we'll figure it out' but Grace always figures it out
Challenge the gender role belief: 'What does a man do? What does a woman do?'
Use team metaphor: 'You're on a baseball team. She's playing shortstop. You say she can play whatever position she wants.'
Ask: 'When was the last substantive money conversation?' (Answer: never in 7 years)
Create urgency: 'Starting a family with this dynamic is not an option'
Set up monthly money meetings with structure
expected_final_outcome: Couple money dynamic diagnosed, avoider/optimizer pattern named, specific recent clash analyzed, commitment to weekly money meetings, urgency created for family planning

forbidden_behaviors.detection_pattern: Chris is the problem|Grace is controlling
here's a budget|let me make a spreadsheet
how does that make you feel|explore your feelings
it's not that bad|you're doing fine
